questions.q: Do you take a fourth shot?
questions.story: You tried the same stock three times this week, and got stopped each time. On Friday it reclaims its flush low again.
choices: No, three tries a week is the max
Yes, a new reclaim is a trigger
Yes, at half size for less risk
No, a stop-out bars any retry
questions.answer: No, three tries a week is the max
questions.why: No. On one stock it's 3 tries a week and 6 a month, max. Each try needs a new trigger, and Friday's reclaim is one. But you've already been wrong three times this week. The stock is telling you something, and the fourth try is where revenge trading starts. Half size doesn't reset the count. Step back and let it set up again next week.
questions.lesson_line: Three tries a week on one name. The fourth waits.

wrong.Yes, at half size for less risk: Half size doesn't reset the count. It's still the fourth try this week.
wrong.Yes, a new reclaim is a trigger: It's a real trigger, but the week's limit still holds. Three tries is the max.
wrong.No, a stop-out bars any retry: Too strict. After a stop-out you can buy again on a new trigger, up to 3 a week.

questions.simple: No. Three tries a week on one stock is the max, and this would be the fourth.

questions.q: On one stock we allow at most 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month.
questions.why: True. A new try needs a new trigger, and the limit is 3 in a week and 6 in a month.
questions.lesson_line: Three a week, six a month, each on a new trigger.

questions.q: A later test of the climax trades below the climax low. What does the Wyckoff school expect?

A fast bounce back to the 20 EMA
A higher low and a strong rally
A confirmed bottom and a new uptrend
questions.why: New lows or prolonged consolidation. If the test goes lower than the climax, expect either.
questions.lesson_line: A test below the climax low means new lows or a long wait.

wrong.A fast bounce back to the 20 EMA: A test below the climax low is a warning, not a bounce signal.
wrong.A higher low and a strong rally: A higher low needs the test to hold above the climax low. This one went under it.
wrong.A confirmed bottom and a new uptrend: A climax must be successfully tested first. A lower test is not a success.

questions.q: What happens now?
questions.story: You bought the reclaim at 92.82 with the stop at 91.41, a few cents under the low of the day you bought. Next morning it opens at 93.75, above that low, then trades through your stop.
choices: You're out, the stop is the exit
Wait for a close under the low
Move the stop lower to give room
Hold, the gap rule sets the stop
questions.answer: You're out, the stop is the exit
questions.why: You're out. The stop is the exit the moment price trades through it. It doesn't wait for a close. Waiting for a close is how a small loss turns into a big one on a day like this. The gap rule doesn't help you either. That's only for a stock that opens under your stop, and this one opened above it. The stop only ever moves up. This one closed at 87.89, way under the stop. Getting out at 91.41 saved you.
questions.lesson_line: The stop is the exit. It doesn't wait for a close.

wrong.Wait for a close under the low: A close isn't the test. Once price trades through the stop, you're out.
wrong.Move the stop lower to give room: The stop only moves up, never down or wider.
wrong.Hold, the gap rule sets the stop: It opened above the low, so there's no gap. The gap rule doesn't apply.

questions.simple: You're out. The stop is the exit as soon as price trades through it, no waiting for a close.

deeper.trap: Two habits break this rule: waiting for a close under the low, and moving the stop to give it room. Both widen the loss you planned. The one exception is a gap. If the stock opens under the stop, the low of the first 30-minute bar becomes the new stop. Past 2R, you're out.

questions.q: What does that breadth reading tell you?
questions.story: The Nasdaq is down five days in a row. T2108, the share of stocks above their own 40-day average, closes at 17%.
choices: Washed out, it backs a flush
Mild, only 17% look weak
Not yet, it has to break 15%
Nothing, price is all that matters
questions.answer: Washed out, it backs a flush

That's the backdrop where a market-wide flush can finally run out of sellers. Bracco noted T2108 broke under its 15% floor only once in 3 years, in the April 2025 crash. So 17% is right down near the floor. It doesn't have to break it. It just tells you to get your list ready for a turn.

wrong.Not yet, it has to break 15%: It doesn't have to break 15%. That floor has broken only once in 3 years.
wrong.Nothing, price is all that matters: Breadth tells you how wide the selling is. That's the backdrop for a flush.

questions.q: Which flush would you rather buy?
questions.story: Two leading stocks flush on heavy volume in different weeks. In one week the index holds above its recent lows. In the other, the index breaks to a new low.
choices: The one with the index holding up
The one with the index breaking down
Both, the index doesn't matter
Neither, the index must be stretched
questions.answer: The one with the index holding up
questions.why: The one with the index holding up. When one leader flushes and the market holds, that's a stock-specific shake. The panic is in that name, and it can snap back fast once sellers run out. When the index is breaking to new lows, the selling is everywhere. Your leader gets dragged down with everything else, however good its flush looked. An index that's itself stretched and washed out can work too. One that's still breaking down is a no for me.
questions.lesson_line: A leader's flush works best when the index is holding up.

wrong.The one with the index breaking down: When the index keeps breaking, the selling isn't done. It drags your stock with it.
wrong.Both, the index doesn't matter: It matters a lot. A leader can't bounce for long while the whole market falls.
wrong.Neither, the index must be stretched: Holding up is fine. Stretched works too. Breaking down is what you avoid.

questions.simple: The one with the index holding up, because a leader can't bounce for long while the whole market breaks.

deeper.counter: Holding up isn't the only good read. An index that is itself stretched and washed out works too. What you avoid is an index breaking down. A new index low on rising volume while you hold is a warning to respect.

reasons: the leader flush setting is held under D-002 and D-004

questions.q: A stock's falling fast, and you're checking for a real burst down, not a slow slide. Which of these is a burst sign?
choices: A gap down on the climax day
A close under the lower band
A deep drop off the 10-day high
Price under the 9 and 20 EMA
questions.answer: A gap down on the climax day
questions.why: A gap down on the climax day. That says the panic carried right through the night. A burst down is our parabolic run in reverse. Straight lower closes, gaps down in a row, bigger down days, volume rising, then a gap on the climax day. Each one says the selling is speeding up, not drifting. The more you see, the stronger the burst. A close under the lower band, the drop off the high and the short averages tell you how stretched it is. They don't tell you it's speeding up.
questions.lesson_line: A burst is selling that speeds up: lower closes, gaps, bigger days, rising volume.

wrong.A close under the lower band: A close under the lower band shows a stretch. It isn't a burst sign.
wrong.A deep drop off the 10-day high: How far it fell is a separate check. A burst is about how fast the selling speeds up.
wrong.Price under the 9 and 20 EMA: Being under the short averages is its own check, not a burst sign.

questions.simple: A gap down on the climax day. It shows the selling speeding up, and that's what a burst is.

reasons: the box count is held under D-002

questions.story: A stock closes lower four days in a row. Each of the last two losses is bigger than the day before, and volume rose on both. Only the flush day opens with a gap down.
questions.q: Run down the burst signs. Which one is missing?
choices: Gaps down two days in a row
Three or more lower closes
Losses growing day to day
Volume up two days running
questions.answer: Gaps down two days in a row
questions.why: Gaps down two days in a row. Only the flush day gapped, so that sign isn't there. Everything else checks out: four lower closes in a row, losses getting bigger, volume rising, and a gap on the climax day. That's still a strong burst. The more signs you see, the stronger it is, and you don't need every one. Running down the list just keeps you honest about what you're looking at.
questions.lesson_line: Run the burst signs one by one. One gap isn't two in a row.

wrong.Losses growing day to day: Each of the last two losses was bigger than the day before. That one's there.
wrong.Three or more lower closes: It closed lower four days in a row. That one's there.
wrong.Volume up two days running: Volume rose on each of the last two days. That one's there.

questions.simple: Two gaps down in a row. Only the flush day gapped, and the rest of the burst is there.

reasons: the box count is held under D-002
